reuse.why: Takes its category set from the shared getCategoriesForBulkBudgetAction like setZero and setBulkNMonthAvg, but re-expresses the income/tracking rule and the expense sign flip itself since the tree has no helper for them.

duplication.why: The income-only-in-tracking guard is repeated (as a .filter) and the expense sign conversion is re-implemented as Math.abs instead of the siblings' negate-when-expense, adding a third variant of these small rules.

placement.why: The action is in budget/actions.ts next to setZero and the average actions and registered in budget/app.ts with mutator(undoable(...)).

scope.why: Only the action, its registration and a test are added.

maintainability.why: Mostly consistent, but the Math.abs sign rule diverges from how sibling actions convert spending to a budget (a net-refund month would be budgeted positive), so the rule now lives in two different forms.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Category selection uses getCategoriesForBulkBudgetAction; the income guard and sign flip have no shared helper in this tree.

disguised_duplication.where: setLastMonthSpending: the sibling loop's 'is_income === 1 && !isTrackingBudget() -> continue' is reshaped into an inverted .filter, and the 'if is_income === 0 negate' sign rule is reshaped into a Math.abs ternary.
